analysis:
The supplied units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 2614-3062) holding historical release notes. The patch adds a v0.10.7 candidate section near the top of the file, which is outside the supplied units. I examined these historical notes against the threat model. They contain no executable code and no configuration, and they do not alter any trust boundary.

Relevant threat IDs: the cache notes at line 2614 (external cache storage, UUID pinning, an on-Mac write ledger) are consistent with the T-041 mitigation text. That mitigation covers CacheVolume validation, encrypted external volumes and the limits on UUID cloning. The App Attest worker and endpoint-resumption notes at lines 2646-2659 match TB-011, T-053 and A-008. They say the changes grant no local trust, extend no proof lifetime and need the matching platform implementation. The automatic official-build registration note at lines 2661-2665 states that runtime Apple proof and revocation remain enforced (T-054).

I found no claim in these units that weakens a documented control. The entries do not broaden the cache TTL, they do not remove per-account salt scoping, and they do not revive plaintext fallbacks.

Limits on this review: the actual v0.10.7 additions are in the patch excerpt, which is truncated and was not supplied as numbered units. The changelog's descriptions of the cluster, tensor-parallel and pairing changes could not be checked against any source code, so their security claims are unverified. A later pass should confirm that the new v0.10.7 text (the cluster pair-update wire and public cluster model declarations) is matched by the threat model, since TB-002 and TB-011 may need updating for the pair-update and cluster-wire changes. Nothing in the supplied lines is a concrete regression.
